_readme: ADVERSARIAL SEED for the Menus group. TEMPORARY - deleted in Step 08.
This is the RICHEST group in the plan: all three regression shapes are present and were
confirmed against the actual repository code, then adversarially re-checked. Menus is also
already MIGRATED (commit 14caf7c9), so its trap sites live in the repositories' .ForView /
.ForViewChildren / .IgnoreEntity calls rather than in AutoMapper profiles.
ID BLOCKS. Chosen so no row's PK ever equals a foreign id it carries - trap 2 is a link row's
own PK leaking into a child's ID, and it is INVISIBLE if the two numbers coincide.
VehicleModel                     6_000_00x
MenuVariant                      6_020_00x
MenuItem                         6_030_00x
MenuItemPart                     6_040_00x
ServiceIntervalGroup             6_050_00x
ServiceInterval                  6_060_00x
MenuPeriodicAvailability         6_070_00x   <- link row (variant x interval)
ReplacementItem                  6_080_00x
ReplacementItemVehicleModel      6_090_00x   <- link row (item x model)
ReplacementItemVehicleModelPart  6_100_00x
ReplacementItemServiceIntervalGroup 6_110_00x <- link row (item x group)
StandaloneReplacementItemGroup   6_120_00x
MenuVersion                      6_130_00x
BrandMapping / LabourRateMapping 6_140_00x / 6_150_00x
TRAP COVERAGE - every one of these was confirmed at a cited line, then re-verified by an
adversarial pass that tried to refute it:
trap1  MenuVariantRepository.cs:72-74  .ForViewChildren(d => d.Items, ...Where(!IsDeleted))
Seeded: variant 6020001 owns MenuItem 6030001 (live) AND 6030002 (SOFT-DELETED).
GET MenuVariant/{6020001} must return ONE item. Two means the predicate was dropped.
trap1  MenuVariantRepository.cs:109  nested .ForChildren(d => d.Parts, ...Where(!IsDeleted)
.OrderBy(SortOrder)). Seeded: item 6030001 owns parts 6040001 (SortOrder 1, live),
6040002 (SortOrder 2, live) and 6040003 (SOFT-DELETED). Carries TWO guarantees - the
filter AND the ordering - so this row set catches either being lost.
trap1  VehicleModelRepository.cs:47 and :57-59  same double guarantee one level deeper, over
ReplacementItemVehicleModel and its Parts. Seeded: model 6000001 has RIVM 6090001
(live) and 6090002 (SOFT-DELETED); RIVM 6090001 owns parts 6100001/2 (live) and
6100003 (SOFT-DELETED).
trap2  MenuVariantRepository.cs:63-65  the ANCHOR trap2. MenuPeriodicAvailability is a LINK
row with its own PK plus MenuVariantID and ServiceIntervalID. The DTO member must
carry the SERVICE INTERVAL's id, not the link row's. Seeded so all three numbers
differ: link 6070001, variant 6020001, interval 6060001. If the wrong one is emitted
it is a well-formed hash id of a REAL row - only a literal comparison catches it.
trap2  VehicleModelRepository.cs:48 and ReplacementItemRepository.cs:29  same shape over
ReplacementItemVehicleModel and ReplacementItemServiceIntervalGroup respectively.
trap2  MenuVariantRepository.cs:82  the two-hop case: MenuItem -> RIVM -> ReplacementItem.
The DTO member is the REPLACEMENT ITEM's id, and there are three wrong answers
available (the item's PK, the RIVM link PK, the vehicle model's). All four numbers
are distinct in this seed.
trap3write  MenuRepository.cs:39  .IgnoreEntity(e => e.BrandID). BrandID is DERIVED in
UpsertAsync from the vehicle model, never taken from the body. Seeded as 4242 on menu
6010001 - a value no derivation could produce - so a readback showing a client-sent
number proves the convention mapper started writing it.
Rows carrying _marker are checked LITERALLY in list bodies by the summary gate. That gate
replaces '> 0 rows', which any demo seed satisfies on its own.
TABLE ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING - a table must follow every table it has a foreign key into.
Keys beginning with _ are harness metadata and are never written to SQL.
UNIQUE INDEXES apply to soft-deleted rows too. A soft-deleted 'duplicate' of a live link
row is rejected by the index, so trap1 link rows must differ in one of the indexed
columns rather than being an exact copy flagged IsDeleted.
A _marker needs a STRING COLUMN to live in. MenuVersion has none (Version + VersionDateTime
only), so it carries no marker - the gate would look for text the row cannot hold.

rows._why: Second group: the link table carries a UNIQUE INDEX on (ReplacementItemID, ServiceIntervalGroupID), which a soft-deleted duplicate still violates. The soft-deleted trap1 link row therefore points here rather than at 6050001.
rows.Name: PARITY-SIG-2 parity interval group two

rows._why: Target of the anchor trap2. Its id - NOT the link row's - must appear on the variant's periodic availability member.
Owns a live and a soft-deleted ReplacementItemVehicleModel link row. GET VehicleModel/{id} must show ONE replacement item, and its ID must be the REPLACEMENT ITEM's, not the link row's.
rows.Name: PARITY-VM parity vehicle model

rows._why: Owns a live and a soft-deleted ReplacementItemServiceIntervalGroup link row (ReplacementItemRepository.cs:27-30 carries trap1 AND trap2 in one .ForView).
rows.Name: PARITY-RI parity replacement item

rows._why: Second item so the two-hop trap2 has a distinct wrong answer available.
rows.Name: PARITY-RI-2 parity replacement item two

rows._why: LINK ROW. PK 6110001 differs from BOTH foreign ids (6080001, 6050001). The DTO must carry the SERVICE INTERVAL GROUP's id.

SOFT-DELETED sibling, pointing at group 6050002 because a unique index on (ReplacementItemID, ServiceIntervalGroupID) rejects a soft-deleted duplicate of the live pair. Must not appear in the ReplacementItem detail body.
LINK ROW, live. PK 6090001 differs from ReplacementItemID 6080001 and VehicleModelID 6000001. The vehicle-model detail body must carry the REPLACEMENT ITEM's id here.
SOFT-DELETED link row - these are soft-deleted by the write path deliberately (VehicleModelRepository.cs:99). Must NOT appear on the vehicle model detail body.
Live part, SortOrder 1. The nested projection guarantees BOTH the IsDeleted filter and this ordering.
Live part, SortOrder 2. Seeded AFTER SortOrder 1 in insertion order but must always render second - if ordering is lost this is where it shows.
SOFT-DELETED part. Must never appear.

BrandID = 4242 is a REPOSITORY-DERIVED column (.IgnoreEntity at MenuRepository.cs:39; UpsertAsync derives it from the vehicle model). 4242 is a value no derivation could produce, so a readback carrying a client-sent number proves the trap fired.
The highest-value row in the group. Owns a live and a soft-deleted MenuItem (trap1), a link row for periodic availability (trap2 anchor), and reaches ReplacementItem two hops out (trap2 two-hop).
rows.Name: PARITY-VARIANT parity variant

rows._why: THE ANCHOR TRAP2 LINK ROW. All three numbers differ: own PK 6070001, MenuVariantID 6020001, ServiceIntervalID 6060001. The variant's detail body must carry the SERVICE INTERVAL's id. Emitting the link PK yields a well-formed hash id of a real row, which only a literal comparison distinguishes from correct.

Live item on variant 6020001. Its ReplacementItemVehicleModelID reaches ReplacementItem two hops out - the DTO member must carry the REPLACEMENT ITEM's id (6080001), not the item's own PK, not the RIVM link PK (6090001), not the vehicle model's (6000001). All four are distinct.
SOFT-DELETED sibling on the SAME variant. This is the row that makes trap1 fire: GET MenuVariant/6020001 must return ONE item. Two means .ForViewChildren's !IsDeleted predicate was lost.
Live part, SortOrder 1.
Live part, SortOrder 2 - the ordering guarantee of the nested projection.
SOFT-DELETED nested part (MenuVariantRepository.cs:109). Must never appear inside the variant detail body.

Plain row so the MenuVersion list body is non-empty. Carries NO _marker: the entity has only Version and VersionDateTime, i.e. no string column a marker could live in, so a marker here could never be matched literally in a list body.
